title: Magnets and Static Electricity
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Magnets and Static Electricity Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Describe magnetic and static (electrostatic) forces as non-contact forces; identify magnetic materials; describe uses of magnets in daily life. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand C: Matter and Energy – Forces Causing Movement)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on magnets, attract and repel, magnetic materials, uses of magnets and static electricity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
key_sub: Magnets pull iron and steel; static charge can also pull light objects.
body_html:
How to think about it

Magnets have a north pole and a south pole.

  • Like poles (N and N) repel; unlike poles (N and S) attract.
  • Magnets attract iron, steel, nickel and cobalt, but not plastic, wood, glass or aluminum.
  • Static electricity is a build-up of charge, like a balloon rubbed on your hair.
Example

Will a magnet pick up an aluminum can?

aluminum is not magnetic

Answer: no

Example

What happens when two north poles meet?

like poles

Answer: they repel

Common mistakes

  • Thinking magnets attract all metals.
  • Thinking bigger magnets are always stronger.
  • Mixing up static electricity and magnetism.
